title: A cancelled repo-contract pack kills the go command but orphans its test binary until the binary's own 20m timeout
summary: runGoTestJSON runs `go test -json` with exec.CommandContext, which kills only the direct `go` process. Measured 2026-09-29 with a throwaway probe: a pack over a 20s test, cancelled at a 4s deadline, returned at 4.006s (realRed=false, err "signal: killed") while its test binary lived on with PPID 1 (`slowprobe.test -test.timeout=20m`). A silent or deadlocked guard suite would keep running until its own -test.timeout (20m). Ship's gate cancels the same way; the build floor's new 120s deadline (repoContractFloorDeadline) makes the path reachable at any handoff whose pack runs past 120s, one orphan per handoff and per correction.
fix: Run the pack's `go` in its own process group and kill the group on cancel (cmd.SysProcAttr Setpgid plus cmd.Cancel sending SIGKILL to -pgid, with WaitDelay as the repo's other launchers use), in a unix/other file split like internal/runlease/pidalive_unix.go and pidalive_other.go, since windows is a release target.
acceptance: A pack cancelled by its context leaves no test binary running (probe: pgrep for the test binary after the cancel is empty)
Ship's gate and the build floor keep their classification: a cancel still names nothing
source: console, 2026-09-29, review follow-up M2 on fix/repo-contract-pack-at-build-exit (deadline probe)
